item.title: 8 Takeaways from Tuesday’s Primaries
item.description: A Democratic primary for governor in Wisconsin remained neck and neck early Wednesday, leaving a national battle between progressive and moderate wings largely unsettled.
item.dc:creator: Patricia Mazzei and Tim Balk
item.media:credit: Jamie Kelter Davis for The New York Times
item.media:description: Francesca Hong and David Crowley

item.title: What to Know About David Crowley, the Democratic Candidate for Wisconsin Governor
item.description: The Milwaukee County executive, who won a tight primary race against Francesca Hong early Wednesday, could become the first Black governor of Wisconsin.
item.dc:creator: Tim Balk
item.media:credit: Jamie Kelter Davis for The New York Times
item.media:description: David Crowley, the Milwaukee County executive, was neck and neck with Francesca Hong as returns were counted on Tuesday evening.

item.title: Peggy Flanagan, a Progressive, Wins the Democratic Senate Primary in Minnesota
item.description: The victory by Minnesota’s lieutenant governor was the latest for the left-wing movement in the Midwest. She could become the first Native woman in the Senate.
item.dc:creator: Tim Balk
item.media:description: Lt. Gov. Peggy Flanagan of Minnesota defeated Representative Angie Craig, a moderate, in the state’s Democratic primary race for Senate.

item.title: Trump Says Secret Service Ordered Air Force One Swap
item.description: Trump claims his secret plane was in more danger than the Air Force One decoy the public thought Trump was flying on.
item.dc:creator: Zolan Kanno-Youngs
item.media:description: President Trump speaking to reporters after landing at Joint Base Andrews on Tuesday.

item.title: Matt Little, a Progressive, Wins a Democratic House Primary in Minnesota
item.description: Mr. Little, a former mayor and state senator, beat two other candidates. He focused on promises of banning corporate money from politics and supporting Medicare for all.
item.dc:creator: Lisa Lerer
item.media:credit: Tim Gruber for The New York Times
item.media:description: Matt Little’s progressive pitch won the endorsement of the Democratic-Farmer-Labor Party, Minnesota’s version of the Democratic Party

item.title: Rebecca Cooke Wins Democratic Primary for Key Wisconsin House Seat
item.description: Ms. Cooke, a three-time congressional candidate, held a huge fund-raising edge in a western Wisconsin race that Democrats consider pivotal to their hopes of flipping the House.
item.dc:creator: Mack Liederman
item.media:description: Rebecca Cooke will face Representative Derrick Van Orden in a general election rematch of their 2024 race.

item.title: Son-in-Law of Sean Duffy Wins G.O.P. House Primary in Northern Wisconsin
item.description: Michael Alfonso, 26, had the support of the transportation secretary and an endorsement from President Trump.
item.dc:creator: Mack Liederman
item.media:description: Michael Alfonso will become the youngest lawmaker in Congress if voters in his deeply Republican district elect him in November.

item.title: Rep. John Larson, a Longtime Lawmaker, Loses a Primary in Connecticut
item.description: In an upset, Luke Bronin, the former mayor of Hartford, won the Democratic nomination, capitalizing on calls for generational change.
item.dc:creator: Lisa Lerer
item.media:description: Luke Bronin outraised Representative John Larson and won the state party’s Democratic endorsement.

item.title: Fighter Jets Intercept Aircraft Over Trump’s Patriot Games in Ohio
item.description: It was at least the fourth time that an aircraft has violated the no-fly zone near President Trump this week.
item.dc:creator: Chris Cameron
item.media:description: President Trump at the Patriot Games in Geneva, Ohio, on Tuesday.

item.title: Areas to Watch in Minnesota’s Senate and Governor Primaries
item.description: Divides in both parties will be on display Tuesday night, particularly in a group of key counties.
item.dc:creator: Evan Reynolds

item.title: Areas to Watch in Wisconsin’s Democratic Primary for Governor
item.description: A race between Francesca Hong and David Crowley could highlight the fault lines between Madison and Milwaukee.
item.dc:creator: Christine Zhang

item.title: Minnesota Primary Election Polling Offers Few Answers in Key Races
item.description: The small group of independent surveys in the Democratic primary for Senate and the Republican primary for governor showed a large share of undecided voters.
item.dc:creator: Caroline Soler
item.media:credit: Jenn Ackerman for The New York Times
item.media:description: Voting in the Powederhorn Park neighborhood of Minneapolis on Tuesday. Minnesota has several key races on Tuesday, including a Democratic primary for Senate and a Republican primary for governor.

item.title: In Wisconsin Governor Primary, Polls Have Shown a Progressive Democrat With a Big Lead
item.description: Francesca Hong, a democratic socialist, has consistently led in a Democratic primary that struggled to settle on a field of candidates.
item.dc:creator: Caroline Soler
item.media:credit: Jamie Kelter Davis for The New York Times
item.media:description: Casting ballots in Madison on Tuesday.

item.title: 5 Things to Know About Francesca Hong, the Progressive Running for Wisconsin Governor
item.description: The state assemblywoman, a democratic socialist, is a chef and former small business owner. Her campaign focused on economic issues.
item.dc:creator: Kellen Browning
item.media:credit: Jenn Ackerman for The New York Times
item.media:description: Francesca Hong has argued that her left-wing beliefs — such as free health care and a pause on data center construction — will resonate across the aisle.

item.title: 5 Things to Know About Tom Tiffany, Republican Gubernatorial Candidate in Wisconsin
item.description: Representative Tom Tiffany is running with President Trump’s backing.
item.dc:creator: Julie Bosman
item.media:credit: Valerie Plesch for The New York Times
item.media:description: Representative Tom Tiffany was expected to easily win the Republican primary for governor of Wisconsin on Tuesday.

item.title: 5 Things to Know About Michael Alfonso, Sean Duffy’s Son-in-Law in Wisconsin’s 7th District Race
item.description: If elected, Mr. Alfonso, 26, would be the youngest member of Congress, thanks in no small part to the support his father-in-law, Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy, and an endorsement from President Trump.
item.dc:creator: Mack Liederman
item.media:description: Michael Alfonso, a candidate for U.S. House in Wisconsin’s 7th congressional district.

item.title: 5 Things to Know About Michele Tafoya, Republican Senate Candidate in Minnesota
item.description: Ms. Tafoya, the favorite to become the state’s Republican nominee for Senate, spent years as an N.F.L. sideline reporter and has leaned into her sports background.
item.dc:creator: Tim Balk
item.media:description: Michele Tafoya has cast herself as a moderate Republican who supports some access to abortion.

item.title: Rubio, Bessent and Miller Traveled on Decoy Plane From Turkey Without Trump
item.description: Some of President Trump’s top officials traveled on the original Air Force One, which the president secretly disembarked.
item.dc:creator: Maggie Haberman
item.media:description: President Trump disembarking from Air Force One after landing at Mildenhall Air Force Base in the United Kingdom last month.

item.title: 5 Things to Know About Peggy Flanagan, Democratic Senate Candidate in Minnesota
item.description: Ms. Flanagan, the progressive lieutenant governor of Minnesota, is a former organizer who could become the first Native American woman in the Senate.
item.dc:creator: Tim Balk
item.media:description: Lt. Gov. Peggy Flanagan is running on a progressive, anti-establishment platform in the Democratic primary race for Senate in Minnesota.

item.title: 5 Things to Know About Angie Craig, Democratic Senate Hopeful in Minnesota
item.description: Ms. Craig, a moderate Democratic congresswoman, flipped a swing House seat in 2018 to become Minnesota’s first openly gay member of Congress.
item.dc:creator: Tim Balk
item.media:description: Representative Angie Craig’s supporters say she would be a strong general-election candidate in a Democratic-leaning state.

item.title: Abdul El-Sayed Deleted Old Posts and Videos Defending ‘Defund’ and Floating an End to Fireworks
item.description: The removed posts from Dr. Abdul El-Sayed, the Democratic nominee for Senate in Michigan, immediately set off Republican attacks.
item.dc:creator: Bayliss Wagner
item.media:description: Dr. Abdul El-Sayed is facing former Representative Mike Rogers in a November contest seen as crucial to control of the Senate.

item.title: Ned Lamont Wins the Democratic Primary for Connecticut Governor
item.description: Josh Elliott, a state representative who mounted a primary challenge, pledged to raise taxes on the rich and take the state on a more progressive path.
item.dc:creator: Neil Vigdor
item.media:description: If Gov. Ned Lamont emerges victorious in the general election in November, he would become one of the longest-serving governors in Connecticut history.

item.title: Darline Graham Advances to the Republican Senate Runoff in South Carolina
item.description: Ms. Graham will face Representative Ralph Norman, a hard-line conservative who had previously run for governor, in the runoff.

item.media:credit: Sean Rayford for The New York Times; Haiyun Jiang/The New York Times
item.media:description: Darline Graham and Ralph Norman are headed to a runoff for the Republican nomination for U.S. Senate in South Carolina.

item.title: With Trump Secretly Evacuated, Imperiled Air Force One Became a Flying Decoy
item.description: In response to a threat against the jet last month, the president was clandestinely removed in a catering container. But the plane was sent into the skies anyway with government employees and reporters onboard.
item.dc:creator: Peter Baker
item.category: US and Israeli Attack on Iran (2026)
item.media:description: Members of the news media and others boarding the plane that President Trump was secretly removed from in Ankara, Turkey, last month.

item.title: 5 Things to Know About Darline Graham, Republican Senate Hopeful in South Carolina
item.description: The sister of Senator Lindsey Graham was endorsed by President Trump to serve out the remainder of his term. Now she is running in a special primary election.
item.dc:creator: Emily Davies
item.media:credit: Sean Rayford for The New York Times
item.media:description: Darline Graham’s interim appointment to the U.S. Senate won wide support in South Carolina, but winning a statewide election may be a tougher test.

item.title: 5 Things to Know About Russell Fry, Republican Senate Candidate in South Carolina
item.description: The two-term Republican congressman, who once interned in the office of Senator Lindsey Graham, has campaigned in part on his youth.
item.dc:creator: Patricia Mazzei
item.media:description: Representative Russell Fry is simultaneously running for his House seat and the Senate seat of the late Lindsey Graham.

item.title: 5 Things to Know About Ralph Norman, Republican Senate Candidate in South Carolina
item.description: The longtime lawmaker, a member of an ultraconservative group of House members, came in third place in the Republican primary for governor this year.
item.dc:creator: Patricia Mazzei
item.media:description: Representative Ralph Norman, one of five candidates for the Republican nomination to replace the late Senator Lindsey Graham, is the vice chairman of the House Freedom Caucus.

item.title: 5 Things to Know About Mark Sanford, Republican Senate Candidate in South Carolina
item.description: The former governor and congressman is a staunch fiscal conservative who repeatedly broke with President Trump on government spending, among other issues.
item.dc:creator: Emily Davies
item.media:description: Mark Sanford is a former governor of South Carolina and current candidate in the special Republican Senate primary election.

item.title: Judge Awards $250,000 to Musician Who Fled Trump-Led Kennedy Center Gig
item.description: The center had sued Chuck Redd when he canceled a free concert last year, citing the addition of the Trump name to the venue. But a judge dismissed the case.
item.dc:creator: Julia Jacobs
item.category: Kennedy, John F, Center for the Performing Arts
item.media:description: Chuck Redd was scheduled to perform at a free Christmas Eve concert. It was canceled after he and other performers backed out.

item.title: When to Expect Results in Wisconsin, Minnesota, South Carolina and Beyond
item.description: Six states are holding elections on Tuesday. The unofficial results will be known late Tuesday or early Wednesday.
item.dc:creator: Taylor Robinson
item.media:credit: Narayan Mahon for The New York Times
item.media:description: Voters in Wisconsin were casting ballots on Tuesday in a variety of primary races, including for governor, where the front-runner for the Democratic nomination is Francesca Hong, a state lawmaker and a democratic socialist.

item.title: Angie Craig Has Cash Edge Over Peggy Flanagan in Minnesota’s Democratic Senate Primary
item.description: Representative Angie Craig has benefited from nearly $10 million in spending from groups whose donors remain hidden, giving her an advantage in her Senate primary against Lt. Gov. Peggy Flanagan.
item.dc:creator: Theodore Schleifer
item.media:description: Representative Angie Craig, a moderate, is trying to beat Lt. Gov. Peggy Flanagan, a progressive, in Minnesota’s Democratic primary race for Senate.

item.title: Democrats Accuse Trump Administration of Stonewalling Major Transit Projects
item.description: Congressional Democrats express concern that the delays involve “political considerations.”
item.dc:creator: Emily Badger
item.media:credit: Kim Raff for The New York Times
item.media:description: Last week, a big commuter rail project in Utah moved closer to a funding agreement, an exception in this Trump term.

item.title: This is how President Trump came to back Darline Graham.
item.dc:creator: Emily Davies
item.media:description: President Trump’s support for Darline Graham, the sister of the late senator Lindsey Graham but a political unknown, is a gamble as Republicans and Democrats battle for control of the House and Senate.

item.media:description: Representative Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez said there was “a political risk” in sharing the information.

item.title: Ex-Marine Robert Gilman, Freed by Russia After 4 Years in Prison, Arrives in the U.S.

item.media:description: Robert Gilman in April. He had been sentenced by a Russian court to 10 years in prison.

item.title: How Iran Adapted Its Attacks as U.S. War Munitions Dwindled
item.description: The Iranian strikes that killed three U.S. soldiers in Jordan show how quickly Iran’s war-fighting skills have evolved, as the Pentagon runs low on interceptors.
item.dc:creator: Eric Schmitt and Helene Cooper
item.category: US and Israeli Attack on Iran (2026)
United States Defense and Military Forces
item.media:description: Iran has become a more skilled adversary as its war against the United States has progressed, learning how to evade U.S. air defenses as it widened the battlefield to include most of the Middle East.

item.title: With El-Sayed’s Victory Comes a Wave of Islamophobia
item.description: As Muslim politicians like Abdul El-Sayed in Michigan have become more prominent, they have experienced considerable bigotry. President Trump said Democrats were electing “jihadists.”
item.dc:creator: Jennifer Medina
item.media:credit: Nick Hagen for The New York Times
item.media:description: Since Dr. Abdul El-Sayed’s victory in the Democratic Senate primary in Michigan last week, Republicans have embraced Islamophobic attacks and falsehoods.

item.title: Trump Picks Project 2025 Co-Author for Role That Would Oversee Any Reflecting Pool Review
item.description: Dennis Kirk, a former adviser to Tulsi Gabbard, is President Trump’s nominee for inspector general for the Interior Department.

item.media:description: The Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool.

item.title: U.S. Says It Revoked More Than 175,000 Visas Under Trump
item.description: Most visas were rescinded over criminal accusations, the State Department said, while some were revoked from people who had celebrated the assassination of Charlie Kirk.
item.dc:creator: Isabella Kwai
item.media:credit: Nathan Howard for The New York Times
item.media:description: The State Department’s release did not include names or details of where people were when their visas were revoked.

item.title: Democrats Plan New Push to Defeat Max Miller in Ohio After Abuse Accusations
item.description: The party’s congressional campaign arm added Mr. Miller’s opponent, Brian Poindexter, to its highly competitive “Red to Blue” list.
item.dc:creator: Emily Davies
item.media:credit: Daniel Lozada for The New York Times
item.media:description: Brian Poindexter is the type of candidate Democrats believe can win over working-class voters who have flocked to President Trump in recent years.

item.title: What to Watch in Tuesday’s Primary Elections in Wisconsin, Minnesota and South Carolina
item.description: The left and the middle continue to battle in Democratic primaries for governor in Wisconsin and Senate in Minnesota. In South Carolina, all eyes are on Darline Graham.
item.dc:creator: Patricia Mazzei
item.media:description: Senator Darline Graham, who was appointed to complete the remainder of the late Senator Lindsey Graham’s term, is also running to succeed her brother for a full term. She faces four others in the special Republican primary.
